promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The Depression and the New Deal

questions.q: In which month and year did the Wall Street Crash occur, marking the onset of the Great Depression?
questions.explain: The New York Stock Exchange collapsed in late October 1929, wiping out share values and triggering the Depression.

questions.q: Who was President of the United States when the Wall Street Crash happened in 1929?
questions.explain: Republican Herbert Hoover had taken office in March 1929, months before the Crash.

questions.q: The shanty towns built by the homeless during the Depression were nicknamed 'Hoovervilles' because...
options: many Americans blamed President Hoover for failing to end their poverty
President Hoover personally paid for building them
they were only built on land owned by Hoover
Hoover had ordered their construction as shelters
questions.explain: The mocking name reflected widespread anger that Hoover's government had done too little to relieve suffering.

questions.q: The main purpose of the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) was to...
options: provide young unemployed men with paid work on conservation projects
regulate the stock market and the banks
questions.explain: The CCC put young men to work planting trees, building parks and preventing soil erosion in return for wages.

questions.q: Roosevelt's New Deal is often summarised by the aims of relief, recovery and...
questions.explain: The 'three Rs' were relief for the needy, recovery of the economy and reform to prevent future depressions.

questions.q: Why did the US Supreme Court create difficulties for the New Deal in 1935-36?
options: it ruled that key agencies such as the NRA and AAA were unconstitutional
it refused to let Roosevelt stand for re-election
it declared the whole New Deal illegal in a single ruling
it abolished the office of President
questions.explain: The conservative Court struck down the NRA (1935) and AAA (1936), prompting Roosevelt's failed attempt to 'pack' the Court.

questions.q: A historian argues that the New Deal did not fully solve unemployment. Which fact best supports this view?
options: Unemployment only fell substantially once rearmament for the Second World War began
The New Deal created no jobs at all
questions.explain: Millions remained jobless throughout the 1930s, and it was wartime production, not the New Deal alone, that ended mass unemployment.

questions.q: In the 1954 case Brown v Board of Education, the Supreme Court ruled that...
options: segregation in state schools was unconstitutional
black Americans could not register to vote
questions.explain: The Court decided that racially segregated 'separate but equal' schooling was inherently unequal and unconstitutional.

questions.q: The Montgomery Bus Boycott of 1955-56 began after the arrest of...
questions.explain: Rosa Parks's arrest for refusing to give up her bus seat sparked the year-long boycott led by Martin Luther King.

questions.q: The significance of the 1957 Little Rock crisis was that it...
options: showed the federal government would use troops to enforce desegregation
ended all segregation in the USA overnight
proved that peaceful protest never worked
questions.explain: President Eisenhower sent federal soldiers to protect the 'Little Rock Nine', demonstrating that Washington would uphold the Brown ruling.

questions.q: Martin Luther King's campaigning was based above all on the principle of...
questions.explain: King drew on Gandhi's example, using peaceful marches, boycotts and sit-ins to expose injustice and win public sympathy.

questions.q: At the 1963 March on Washington, Martin Luther King delivered which famous speech?
questions.explain: King's 'I Have a Dream' speech at the Lincoln Memorial became the defining moment of the March on Washington.

questions.q: A congressman in 1964 wants a national law banning discrimination in restaurants, hotels and employment on the grounds of race. Which measure achieved this?
questions.explain: The 1964 Civil Rights Act outlawed racial discrimination in public places and employment across the USA.

questions.q: At the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, two black American athletes raised a single gloved fist on the medal podium. This gesture is best understood as...
options: a Black Power salute protesting against racial injustice
a celebration of the New Deal
questions.explain: Tommie Smith and John Carlos used the raised-fist Black Power salute to draw global attention to racism in America.

questions.q: Compared with Martin Luther King, the early Malcolm X was more likely to...
options: reject nonviolence and support black self-reliance and separation
demand immediate integration through peaceful marches
questions.explain: As a Nation of Islam spokesman, Malcolm X rejected integration and nonviolence, calling for black self-defence and self-reliance.

questions.q: The political scandal that forced President Richard Nixon to resign in 1974 was known as...
questions.explain: The Watergate cover-up, following a break-in at the Democratic headquarters, led Nixon to resign in August 1974.

questions.q: Betty Friedan's influential 1963 book, which helped launch the modern women's movement, was titled...
questions.explain: The Feminine Mystique challenged the idea that women should be confined to home life and inspired 1960s feminism.

questions.q: The Equal Rights Amendment (ERA), intended to guarantee equal rights regardless of sex, ultimately failed because...
options: it was not ratified by enough states
the Supreme Court declared women's rights illegal
questions.explain: Although passed by Congress, the ERA fell short of the required number of state ratifications and never became law.

questions.q: The 1973 Supreme Court case Roe v Wade concerned a woman's legal right to...
questions.explain: Roe v Wade established a constitutional right to abortion, a landmark decision for the women's movement.

questions.q: In the early 1970s a campaigner demands equal pay, access to contraception and an end to sex discrimination. She is most closely associated with...
questions.explain: These demands were central to the Women's Liberation (feminist) movement that grew rapidly in the USA during the 1960s and 1970s.
